The total prize fund will be an increased total of £750,000, with the winner receiving £130,000.

rows.title: 2026 Silver Rail Elementary School shooting
rows.description: Mass shooting in Oregon, US
rows.summary: On October 15, 2026, a school shooting occurred at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, United States. The perpetrator, 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, made entry into the school by jumping over a school fence before shooting through glass panels of a locked door with a pump-action shotgun. John then entered a special education classroom, where four adults and five children were inside at the time, and fatally shot three children and a teacher and injured another student and a teaching assistant before he was shot and killed by 36-year-old Kaylub Giamanco, an armed civilian with a concealed carry permit and father of two students at the school, who had followed John into the school after seeing him shoot his way into the building.

rows.title: 2026 United States House of Representatives elections
rows.description: House elections for the 120th U.S. Congress
rows.summary: The 2026 United States House of Representatives elections were held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, as part of the 2026 midterm elections during President Donald Trump's second, nonconsecutive term. Voters elected representatives from all 435 congressional districts across each of the fifty U.S. states, and five of the six non-voting delegates from the District of Columbia and the inhabited U.S. territories.

rows.title: 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa
rows.summary: The 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa were held on November 3, 2026, to elect the four U.S. representatives from the state of Iowa, one from each of the state's congressional districts. The elections coincided with other elections to the House of Representatives, elections to the United States Senate, and various state and local elections. The primary elections took place on June 2, 2026.

rows.title: 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Michigan
rows.summary: The 2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Michigan were held on November 3, 2026, to elect the 13 U.S. representatives from the state of Michigan, one from all the state's congressional districts. The elections coincided with other elections to the House of Representatives, elections to the United States Senate, and various state and local elections. The primary elections took place on August 4, 2026. The filing deadline to run for the August 4 primary was April 21.

rows.title: 2026 United States Senate election in Maine
rows.summary: The 2026 United States Senate election in Maine was held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the United States Senate to represent the state of Maine. Democratic former state Senate president Troy Jackson defeated Republican incumbent Susan Collins. The election was conducted with ranked-choice voting.

rows.title: 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi
rows.summary: The 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi was held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the United States Senate to represent the state of Mississippi. Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith is seeking re-election to a second full term. She is being challenged by Democratic district attorney Scott Colom.

rows.title: 2026 United States Senate election in Texas
rows.summary: The 2026 United States Senate election in Texas was held on November 3, 2026, to elect the Class 2 member of the United States Senate from the state of Texas. Democratic state representative James Talarico defeated Republican state attorney general Ken Paxton.

rows.title: 2026 United States gubernatorial elections
rows.summary: Gubernatorial elections were held in the United States on November 3, 2026. These elections took place in 36 states and three territories. The previous gubernatorial elections for this group of states took place in 2022, except in New Hampshire and Vermont, where governors serve two-year terms and elected their governors in 2024.

rows.title: 2026 United States judicial elections
rows.summary: United States judicial elections are scheduled to be held in 2026, in various states and territories across the country, for both supreme courts and appellate courts. Justices are elected across the country in partisan, nonpartisan, and retention elections.

rows.title: 2026 United States state legislative elections
rows.summary: The 2026 United States state legislative elections were held on November 3, 2026, for 88 state legislative chambers in 46 states. Across the fifty states, approximately 60% of upper house seats and 92% of lower house seats will be up for election. Additionally, six territorial chambers will be up in four territories and the District of Columbia. These elections will take place concurrently with other state and local elections, including gubernatorial elections in multiple states.

rows.title: 2026 anti-CEC protests

rows.title: 2026 in rock music

rows.title: 2026–27 AFC Bournemouth season
rows.description: 125th season in existence of AFC Bournemouth
rows.summary: The 2026–27 season is the 125th season in the history of AFC Bournemouth and the club's fifth consecutive season in the Premier League, making it their tenth season in the top flight overall. In addition to the domestic league, the club are participating in the FA Cup, the EFL Cup and the UEFA Europa League, the latter being the club's first ever participation in European competition.

rows.title: 2026–27 Brighton & Hove Albion F.C. season
rows.description: 125th season in existence of Brighton & Hove Albion FC
rows.summary: The 2026–27 season is the 125th season in the history of Brighton & Hove Albion, and their tenth consecutive season in the Premier League. In addition to the domestic league, the club also participate in the FA Cup, the EFL Cup, and the UEFA Conference League, the latter being their first season back in a European competition since the 2023–24 campaign.

rows.title: 2026–27 Indian Super League
rows.description: Football league season in India
rows.summary: The 2026–27 Indian Super League, also known as the MG Indian Super League, is the 13th season of the Indian Super League (ISL) and the 31st season of top-tier Indian football. The season began on 10 October 2026. Sony Sports and Google have acquired the league's media rights for the next two seasons. Sony Sports holds the satellite television rights for the Indian subcontinent, and streams matches on SonyLIV in India, while Google streams every match live on YouTube in India and worldwide.

rows.title: 2026–27 Premier League Cup
rows.description: Football tournament season
rows.summary: The 2026–27 Premier League Cup is the thirteenth edition of the competition. A new format for 2026/27 was made for the competition, with 40 teams divided into 10 groups of four. Each side plays the other three teams home and away, with the 10 group winners and six best runners-up advancing to the Round of 16. This is 8 clubs more than last time after contracting back to 32 last season. 4 academies that participated last season did not return this year. Last year's runners up and inaugural participant Sunderland did not return after 12 consecutive seasons in the competition, Colchester United after 10 consecutive seasons, Watford did not return after 2 consecutive seasons, and finally Leyton Orient did not return after playing last year. In terms of teams returning to the competition, 10 teams came back. Bolton Wanderers and Gillingham return for the first time since the competition was a knockout only in 2015–16, West Ham United returns after a 5 season absence, Plymouth Argyle is returning for the after a 4 year absence since 2022–23, Newcastle United and Peterborough United returned after a 2 year absence, and Brighton & Hove Albion, Fleetwood Town, Huddersfield Town, Leeds United, and Southampton returned after missing last year's competition. Wycombe Wanderers is participating in the competition for the very first time.

rows.title: 2026–27 S.L. Benfica season
rows.description: Benfica 2026–27 football season
rows.summary: The 2026–27 Sport Lisboa e Benfica season is the club's 123rd season in existence and its 93rd consecutive season in the top flight of Portuguese football. Domestically, Benfica plays in the Primeira Liga, and also compete in the Taça da Liga and Taça de Portugal. In Europe, Benfica plays in the UEFA Europa League.

rows.title: 2026–27 UEFA Europa League league phase
rows.description: International football club competition in Europe
rows.summary: The 2026–27 UEFA Europa League league phase began on 16 September 2026 and will end on 28 January 2027. A total of 36 teams are competing in the league phase to decide the 24 places in the knockout phase of the 2026–27 UEFA Europa League.

rows.title: 2028 Democratic Party presidential primaries
rows.description: Selection of the Democratic Party nominee
rows.summary: Presidential primaries and caucuses will be organized by the Democratic Party to select delegates to the 2028 Democratic National Convention to determine the party's nominee for president in the 2028 election. The primaries and caucuses will take place in all 50 U.S. states, in the District of Columbia, in five U.S. territories, and through Democrats Abroad.

rows.title: 2028 European Men's Handball Championship qualification
rows.summary: The 2028 European Men's Handball Championship qualification tournament is a Handball competition that was played from January 2025 to 9 May 2027 to determine the 20 EHF member men's national teams that will join the automatically qualified teams in the final tournament. Alongside the qualifiers, the EHF Euro Cup also takes place.

rows.title: 2028 Republican Party presidential primaries
rows.description: Selection of the Republican Party nominee
rows.summary: Presidential primaries and caucuses are going to be organized by the Republican Party to select delegates to the 2028 Republican National Convention to determine the party's nominee for president in the 2028 election. The primaries and caucuses will take place in all 50 U.S. states, Washington, D.C., and five U.S. territories. No primary dates have been determined.

rows.title: AS Adema 149–0 SO l'Emyrne
rows.description: Football match
rows.summary: AS Adema 149–0 SO l'Emyrne was an association football match that took place in Toamasina, Madagascar on 31 October 2002. It holds the world record for the highest scoreline in football history, as recognised by The Guinness Book of Records. Stade Olympique de l'Emyrne (SOE) intentionally lost to rivals AS Adema in a self-orchestrated protest over unfavourable refereeing decisions in a previous match that cost them the national championship. Prior to that day, the previous highest scoreline was 36–0 to Arbroath F.C. over Bon Accord F.C. in the Scottish Cup in 1885.

rows.title: Across the Universe
rows.description: 1969 song by the Beatles
rows.summary:
"Across the Universe" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles. It was written by John Lennon and credited to Lennon–McCartney. The song first appeared on the 1969 various artists' charity compilation album No One's Gonna Change Our World and later, in a different form, on their 1970 album Let It Be, the group's final released studio album. The original version featured on two different albums both titled Rarities: a 1978 British release and a 1980 US release. It was also included on their 1988 album Past Masters, Volume Two.
The song has been covered by many artists, including David Bowie on his 1975 album Young Americans, which featured contributions from Lennon.

rows.title: Aiham Ousou
rows.description: Syrian footballer (born 2000)
rows.summary: Aiham Hanz Ousou is a professional footballer who plays as a centre-back for Belgian club Charleroi. Born in Sweden, he plays for the Syria national team.

rows.title: Alan Jones (racing driver)
rows.description: Australian racing driver (1946–2026)
rows.summary: Alan Stanley Jones was an Australian racing driver and broadcaster who competed in Formula One between 1975 and 1986. Jones won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 1980 with Williams, and won 12 Grands Prix across 10 seasons.

rows.title: Alessandro Staccioli
rows.description: Italian Roman Catholic bishop (1931–2026)
rows.summary: Alessandro Staccioli was an Italian Roman Catholic prelate who served as Auxiliary Bishop of the Archdiocese of Siena–Colle di Val d'Elsa–Montalcino from 1975 to 1990. He previously served as Vicar Apostolic of Luang Prabang in Laos from 1968 until the expulsion of missionaries in 1975.

rows.title: Algospeak
rows.description: Obfuscated speech on social media
rows.summary: On social media, algospeak is a self-censorship phenomenon in which users adopt coded expressions to evade real or imagined automated content moderation. It allows users to discuss topics deemed sensitive to moderation algorithms while avoiding penalties such as shadow banning, downranking, or de-monetization of content. A type of netspeak, algospeak primarily serves to bypass censorship, though it can also reinforce group belonging, especially in marginalized communities. Algospeak has been identified as one source of linguistic change in the modern era, with some terms spreading into everyday offline speech and writing. The term has been used more broadly to include any language change driven by digital usage.

rows.title: Ali-Asghar Fani
rows.description: Iranian politician and former Minister of Education (1953/1954–2026)
rows.summary: Ali Asghar Fani was an Iranian politician who served as Minister of Education. He took the office as acting minister on 23 August 2013 after parliament rejected nominated Mohammad-Ali Najafi for the post. Fani was officially nominated for the post by President Hassan Rouhani and was voted for by the parliament. He resigned from his position on 19 October 2016, as part of President Rouhani's cabinet reshuffling. Fani had previously served as acting minister in 2005. He died on 5 November 2026, at the age of 72.

rows.title: All Dogs Go to Heaven
rows.description: 1989 animated film directed by Don Bluth
rows.summary: All Dogs Go to Heaven is a 1989 animated musical fantasy comedy drama film directed by Don Bluth. It stars the voices of Loni Anderson, Judith Barsi, Dom DeLuise, Melba Moore, Charles Nelson Reilly, Burt Reynolds, and Vic Tayback. Set in New Orleans in 1939, it tells the story of Charlie B. Barkin, a German Shepherd mix who is murdered by his former friend, Carface Carruthers. Charlie escapes from Heaven to return to Earth, where his best friend, Itchy Itchiford, still lives, to take revenge on Carface. Instead, he befriends a young orphan girl named Anne-Marie. In the process, Charlie learns an important lesson about kindness, friendship, and love.

rows.title: Alp Supply Co.
rows.description: Nicotine and caffeiene pouch company
rows.summary: Alp is a brand of nicotine and caffeine pouches created by Tucker Carlson and Turning Point Brands, a subsidiary of American conservative group Turning Point USA. Alp pouches are designed to be placed between the lip and gums of the user, allowing the product to be to be absorbed into the bloodstream through oral soft tissue.

rows.title: Ampato
rows.description: Dormant stratovolcano in southern Peru
rows.summary: Ampato is a dormant 6,288-metre (20,630 ft) stratovolcano in the Andes of southern Peru. It lies about 70–75 kilometres (43–47 mi) northwest of Arequipa and is part of a north-south chain that includes the volcanoes Hualca Hualca and Sabancaya, the last of which has been historically active.

rows.title: Andar (Pashtun tribe)
rows.description: Ghilji Pashtun tribe
rows.summary: The Andar are a Ghilji Pashtun sub-tribe. The Andar occupy nearly the whole of the extensive district of Shalgar south of Ghazni.

rows.title: Archie E. Mitchell
rows.description: American evangelical and missionary (born 1918)
rows.summary: The Reverend Archie Emerson Mitchell was an American minister with the Christian and Missionary Alliance (C&MA). Mitchell Recreation Area was built after his pregnant wife and five Sunday school children died from Fu-Go balloon bombs in the only war-related deaths in the American continent in World War II. Mitchell served as a missionary to South Vietnam working on the staff of the Ban Me Thuot Leprosarium when he was taken captive by the Vietcong on May 30, 1962, along with Daniel Amstutz Gerber and Eleanor Ardel Vietti. None of the three have been seen since.

rows.title: Armenians in Indonesia
rows.description: Ethnic group
rows.summary: Many Armenian merchants from Amsterdam, Isfahan and Madras went to Southeast Asia, particularly the Dutch East Indies in the 19th century to trade, and to set up factories and plantations. Armenian merchants settled in parts of Java, then part of the Dutch East Indies.

rows.title: Australian Professional Leagues
rows.description: Operator of commercial soccer competitions in Australia
rows.summary: The Australian Professional Leagues (APL) is the governing body for the A-League Men, A-League Women, and A-League Youth, known collectively as the A-Leagues.

rows.title: Autism
rows.description: Condition involving social and behavioral differences
rows.summary: Autism, also known as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), is a condition characterized by impairment in social communication and interaction, as well as a need or strong preference for predictability and routine, sensory processing differences, focused interests, or repetitive behaviors. Features of autism are present from early childhood and the condition typically persists throughout life. Autism is classified as a neurodevelopmental disorder, and a diagnosis requires professional assessment that these characteristics cause significant challenges in daily life beyond what is expected given a person's age and social environment. Because autism is a spectrum disorder, presentations vary and support needs range from minimal assistance to full-time, 24-hour care.

rows.title: Awka North
rows.description: LGA in Anambra State, Nigeria
rows.summary: Awka North is a Local Government Area in Anambra State, south-central Nigeria. Towns that make up the local government are Awba Ofemili, Ugbenu, Ugbene, Ebenebe, Achalla, Urum, Amansea, Amanuke, Isu Aniocha, Mgbakwu. This Local Government Area falls under the Anambra North senatorial district of Anambra State. The headquarters of this LGA is located at Achalla. At the 2006 census, this LGA had a total population of 112,192 people.

rows.title: Badminton at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics
rows.summary: The badminton tournaments at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics was held from 1 to 5 November. The events took place at Dakar Arena in Diamniadio, Senegal. The maximum age of participants would be 17 years old up to the closing ceremony of the Games.

rows.title: Badminton at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics – Men's singles
rows.description: Badminton championships
rows.summary: The men's singles badminton tournament at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics was held between 1–5 November at the Dakar Arena. The draw was announced at 30 October 2026.

rows.title: Bangladesh national football team
rows.description: Men's association football team
rows.summary: The Bangladesh national football team is the national recognised football team of Bangladesh and is controlled by the Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF), the governing body for football in Bangladesh, formed in 1972. Bangladesh became a member of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) in 1973 and FIFA in 1976.

rows.title: Barbara Bagshaw
rows.description: American politician
rows.summary: Barbara Bagshaw is an American politician who served as a member of the Maine House of Representatives for Maine's 106th House district from December 7, 2022 until her defeat in the November 3, 2026 election to Bradley Youngs.

rows.title: Battle of Midway
rows.description: 1942 major naval battle in World War II
rows.summary: The Battle of Midway was a major naval battle in the Pacific Theater of World War II that took place on 4–7 June 1942, six months after Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor and one month after the Battle of the Coral Sea. The Japanese Combined Fleet under the command of Isoroku Yamamoto suffered a decisive defeat by two carrier strike groups of the U.S. Pacific Fleet near Midway Atoll, about 1,300 mi northwest of Oahu. Yamamoto had intended to capture Midway and lure out and destroy the U.S. Pacific Fleet, especially the aircraft carriers which had escaped damage at Pearl Harbor.

rows.title: Ben Adams
rows.description: British musical artist (born 1981)
rows.summary: Ben Adams is a British singer and songwriter from Ascot, England. He represented Norway in the Eurovision Song Contest 2022 along with Gaute Ormåsen as a part of pop band Subwoolfer. He is also known as the lead singer of the British-Norwegian boy band A1.

rows.title: Ben Nighthorse Campbell
rows.description: American politician (1933–2025)
rows.summary: Ben Nighthorse Campbell was an American politician and United States Air Force veteran who served in both chambers of the United States Congress, representing Colorado's 3rd congressional district in the United States House of Representatives from 1987 to 1993 and as a member of the United States Senate from 1993 to 2005. He served as one of the 44 members of the Council of Chiefs of the Cheyenne people. During his time in office, he was the only Native American serving in Congress. He was the last Native American elected to the U.S. Senate until the 2022 election of Markwayne Mullin.

rows.title: Betel
rows.description: Species of plant
rows.summary: Betel is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia. It is an evergreen, dioecious vine, with glossy heart-shaped leaves and white catkins. Betel plants are cultivated for their leaves, which are most commonly used as flavoring for chewing with areca nut in so-called betel quid, which is carcinogenic, contains a psychostimulant drug, and is associated with a wide range of serious health conditions.

rows.title: Big Brother (British TV series) series 23
rows.description: Season of television series
rows.summary: Big Brother 2026, also known as Big Brother 23, was the twenty-third series of Big Brother. It was the fourth civilian series of Big Brother to air on ITV2 after ITV plc gained the rights to the format, and the sixth series to air on the network overall. The series began on 13 September 2026 and was again co-presented by AJ Odudu and Will Best. At 54 days, it was the longest series to air since the eighteenth series on Channel 5 in 2017, and the longest to air on ITV overall.

rows.title: Billy Bounce
rows.description: Comic strip
rows.summary: Billy Bounce was a comic strip published by noted illustrator W. W. Denslow (1901–1902) and later C. W. Kahles (1902–1905) between November 10, 1901, and December 3, 1905, with a series of reprints in 1908 and 1909. The strip centers on the actions of the title character, a ball-shaped boy who is capable of bouncing long distances. It is noted as one of the earliest comic strips in which the protagonist has superpowers.

rows.title: Bogdan Perzynski
rows.description: Polish artist
rows.summary: Bogdan P. K. Perzyński is a contemporary artist who lives and works in Austin, Texas.

rows.title: Capital punishment in California
rows.summary: Capital punishment is a legal penalty in the U.S. state of California. However, the penalty has not been carried out in that state since 2006, due to a standing federal court order issued that year against the practice when using lethal injection not administered by trained medical staff, and a 2019 moratorium on executions ordered by Governor Gavin Newsom. The litigation resulting in the court order has been on hold since the promulgation of the moratorium. Should the moratorium end and the freeze conclude, executions could resume under the current state law.

rows.title: Caramilk
rows.description: Chocolate brand by Cadbury
rows.summary: Caramilk is a brand name used for two distinct chocolate bar products made by Cadbury. The Canadian version of Caramilk is a milk chocolate bar filled with caramel and it was introduced in 1938. In Australia the Caramilk brand is used for a caramelised white chocolate bar.

rows.title: Clown Motel
rows.description: Clown-themed motel in Tonopah, Nevada, US
rows.summary: The Clown Motel is a clown-themed motel along north Main Street in Tonopah, Nevada, which has been referred to as "America's scariest motel". The building is located adjacent to the historic Tonopah Cemetery, where the father of the original owners is buried.

rows.title: Convection oven
rows.description: Appliance that heats food
rows.summary: A convection oven is an oven that has fans to circulate air around food to create an evenly heated environment. In an oven without a fan, natural convection circulates hot air unevenly, so that it will be cooler at the bottom and hotter at the top than in the middle. Fan ovens cook food faster, and are also used in non-food, industrial applications. Small countertop convection ovens for household use are often marketed as air fryers.

rows.title: Count Dankula
rows.description: Scottish YouTuber (born 1987)
rows.summary: Mark Meechan, better known as Count Dankula, is a Scottish YouTuber, comedian, and former candidate for the European Parliament.

rows.title: CounterPunch
rows.description: Bi-monthly left-wing online magazine based in Petrolia, California
rows.summary: CounterPunch is a left-wing online magazine. Content includes a free section published five days a week, as well as a subscriber-only area called CounterPunch+, where original articles are published weekly. CounterPunch is based in the United States and covers politics in a manner its editors describe as "muckraking with a radical attitude".

rows.title: Country Club of Fairfield
rows.description: Private golf club in Connecticut
rows.summary: The Country Club of Fairfield is a private golf and country club on Sasco Hill Road in the Southport section of Fairfield, Connecticut, on the shore of Long Island Sound beside Southport Harbor. Founded in 1914 by financier Oliver Gould Jennings and a group of friends, the club opened its 18-hole course in 1921. The course was laid out by Seth Raynor and later altered by A. W. Tillinghast, Robert Trent Jones Sr., Geoffrey Cornish and, most recently, restoration architect Bruce Hepner. The Country Club of Fairfield has consistently been ranked as a top course in Connecticut.

rows.title: Courthouse facility dog
rows.summary: In the United States, a courthouse facility dog is a professionally trained facility dog that has graduated from an accredited assistance dog organization that is a member of Assistance Dogs International. Such dogs assist crime victims, witnesses and others during the investigation and prosecution of crimes, as well as during other legal proceedings. Courthouse facility dogs also provide assistance to Drug Court and Mental Health Court participants during their recovery from drugs, alcohol, mental illness and posttraumatic stress disorder.

rows.title: Cyclone Murasu
rows.description: North Indian Ocean cyclone in 2026
rows.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu was a robust tropical cyclone that affected South India. It is the ninth depression and the second cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season after Cyclone Arnab, which also battered the south-eastern coast of India less than a week before. Traversing the Bay of Bengal east to west, the system originated as a low-pressure area over Andaman Sea on 29 October 2026 at the same time Arnab's remnants were dissipating inland.

rows.title: Daegu iM Bank Park
rows.description: Football stadium in Daegu, South Korea
rows.summary: Daegu iM Bank Park (Korean: 대구iM뱅크파크), known as the Daegu Forest Arena (Korean: 대구포레스트아레나) in the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) international matches, is a football-specific stadium located in Daegu, South Korea, and is the home stadium of the K League 2 club Daegu FC. The stadium opened in March 2019 and has a seating capacity of 12,419 spectators.

rows.title: Daulatpur–Saturia tornado
rows.description: 1989 tornado in Bangladesh
rows.summary: The Daulatpur–Saturia tornado was a violent tornado that occurred in Manikganj District, Bangladesh on April 26, 1989. While it was destructive and extremely deadly, there is great uncertainty about the death toll. Official estimates from the World Meteorological Organization indicate that it killed approximately 1,300 people, which would make it the deadliest tornado in history. The tornado affected the cities of Daulatpur and Saturia the most, moving east through Daulatpur and eventually northeast into Saturia. Previously, the area that the tornado hit had been in a state of drought for six months.

rows.title: Death Battle
rows.description: American web series
rows.summary: Death Battle is an American animated web series about battleboarding. Originally published by the website ScrewAttack in 2010, the show has changed considerably over its history. It is the longest-running web series in the battleboarding genre, and has gained a cult following.

rows.title: Deaths in 2026
rows.summary: The following notable deaths occurred in 2026. Names are reported under the date of death, in alphabetical order. A typical entry reports information in the following sequence:Name, age, country of citizenship at birth, subsequent nationality, what subject was noted for, cause of death, and a reference.

rows.title: Dian McCarthy
rows.description: American politician
rows.summary: Dian McCarthy is an American politician. A member of the Democratic Party, she is the member-elect for the 16th District of the New Hampshire Senate. McCarthy previously served as the chair of the Goffstown School Board.

rows.title: Don Leonard (politician)
rows.description: American politician
rows.summary: Don Ralph Leonard is an American politician. A member of the Democratic Party, he is the representative-elect for Ohio's 15th congressional district in the United States House of Representatives, being elected in the 2026 election.

rows.title: Douglas W. Owsley
rows.description: American anthropologist (born 1951)
rows.summary: Douglas W. Owsley is an American anthropologist who is the curator of Biological Anthropology at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History (NMNH). He is a respected and well-known forensic anthropologist and archaeologist who has been involved in several high-profile investigations. In September 2001, he provided scientific analysis at the military mortuary located at Dover Air Force Base, following the 9/11 attack in Washington, D.C. The following year, the US Department of Defense honored him with the Commander's Award for Civilian Service for helping in the identification of 60 federal and civilian victims who died when American Airlines Flight 77 hit the Pentagon.

rows.title: Early life of Néstor Kirchner
rows.summary: Néstor Carlos Kirchner was an Argentine politician who served as the 54th President of Argentina from 25 May 2003 until 10 December 2007. He was born in Río Gallegos, and moved to La Plata to attend university. As a student, he was very politically active, but left the city and returned to Patagonia at the start of the Dirty War.

rows.title: East Atlantic Biosphere Reserve Network
rows.summary: The East Atlantic Biosphere Reserve Network (REDBIOS) is an interregional network established in 1994 within UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme (MAB). It connects biosphere reserves in the Macaronesian region and parts of West Africa, including the Canary Islands (Spain), the Azores and Madeira (Portugal), Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Mauritania, Morocco, Senegal, and São Tomé and Príncipe. The network promotes cooperation and the exchange of knowledge and experience among biosphere reserves. Its activities focus on biodiversity conservation, the sustainable use of natural resources, environmental education, and sustainable development, particularly in island and coastal areas.

rows.title: Ellen Ochoa
rows.description: American astronaut and engineer (born 1958)
rows.summary: Ellen Ochoa is an American engineer, former astronaut and former director of the Johnson Space Center. In 1993, Ochoa became the first Latina to go to space when she served on a nine-day mission aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery. Ochoa became director of the center upon the retirement of the previous director, Michael Coats, on December 31, 2012. She was the first Latina director and the second female director of Johnson Space Center.

rows.title: Elora Shehabuddin
rows.description: Scholar of gender and women's studies

rows.summary: Erin Pauling Paré is an American politician who is a Republican member of the North Carolina General Assembly. Paré represents the state's 37th House district.

rows.title: Fasman Yeshiva High School
rows.description: High school and yeshiva located in Skokie, Illinois
rows.summary: Fasman Yeshiva High School, known colloquially as Skokie Yeshiva, is an Orthodox Jewish all-boys high school in Skokie, Illinois. Fasman Yeshiva offers a dual curriculum of secular and Judaic studies.

rows.title: Francesco di Maria
rows.description: Italian Baroque painter (1623–1690)
rows.summary: Francesco di Maria (1623–1690) was an Italian painter of the Baroque period, active mainly in Naples. A dedicated pupil of Domenichino, di Maria became the most fervent champion and defender of classicism, strict draftsmanship (disegno), and rigorous composition in Naples during the second half of the 17th century. Di Maria is famous for his fierce academic rivalry with his contemporary, Luca Giordano. While Giordano championed a rapid, brilliant, and color-driven early Rococo style, di Maria defended his master's Baroque classicism.

rows.title: François Letexier
rows.description: French football referee (born 1989)
rows.summary: François Letexier is a French football referee who has officiated in Ligue 1 since January 2016. He has been a FIFA referee since 2017 and is ranked as a UEFA elite category referee. Letexier has taken charge in every major UEFA club and international-level tournament. He is also the youngest referee to officiate a UEFA Euro final, as he took charge of the UEFA Euro 2024 final when he was 35 years old.

rows.title: Fred Forest
rows.description: French artist (1933–2026)
rows.summary: Fred Forest was a French new media artist who made use of video, photography, the printed press, mail, radio, television, telephone, telematics, and the internet in a wide range of installations, performances, and public interventions that explore both the ramifications and potential of media space. He was a co-founder of both the Sociological Art Collective (1974) and the Aesthetics of Communication movement (1983).

rows.title: Frozen yogurt
rows.description: Frozen dairy dessert
rows.summary: Frozen yogurt is a frozen dessert made with yogurt or other dairy and non-dairy products. Frozen yogurt is similar in composition to ice cream, with its main ingredient being milk or milk substitutes.

rows.title: Galapagos penguin
rows.description: Species of bird
rows.summary: The Galápagos penguin is a penguin endemic to the Galápagos Islands of Ecuador. It is the only penguin found north of the equator. Most inhabit Fernandina Island and the west coast of Isabela Island. The cool waters of the Humboldt and Cromwell Currents allow it to survive despite the tropical latitude. The Galápagos penguin is one of the banded penguins, the other species of which live mostly on the coasts of Africa and mainland South America. Due to their warm environment, Galápagos penguins have developed techniques to stay cool. The feathers on their back, flippers, and head are black, and they have a white belly and a stripe looping from their eyes down to their neck and chin. Each penguin keeps only one mate, and breeds year-round. Because there are no soft areas to nest, their nests are typically in caves and crevices which also provide protection against predators and the harsh environment. The Galápagos penguin has a lifespan of 20 years, but due to predation, life expectancy in the wild could be significantly reduced. They have been critically impacted to the point of endangerment by climate change and pollution caused by plastic waste due to tourism and urbanization.

rows.title: Genshin Impact
rows.description: 2020 video game
rows.summary: Genshin Impact  is a 2020 action role-playing video game developed and published by miHoYo. It is distributed outside China by miHoYo's international subsidiary Cognosphere, also known as HoYoverse. At its core, the game features an anime style, open-world environment, an action-focused battle system consisting of elemental magic with character-switching, and a mythical main story. Genshin Impact is a free-to-play game monetized through gacha mechanics, which is updated regularly using the games as a service model. It was originally released for Android, iOS, PlayStation 4, and Windows, followed by the PlayStation 5 in 2021, and Xbox Series X/S in 2024. In China, a native port for HarmonyOS NEXT was released in September 2025. Support for PlayStation 4 was removed in April 2026.

rows.title: George Holmes (vice-chancellor)
rows.description: British academic administrator (born 1961)
rows.summary: George Edward Thomas Holmes is a former British academic administrator, previously serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Greater Manchester from 2006 to 2025.

rows.description: Left million to Lake Forest College
rows.summary: Grace Groner was an American woman recognized after her death for a posthumous gift of seven million dollars to her alma mater, Lake Forest College.

rows.title: Grinds Pouches
rows.description: Caffeine pouch brand
rows.summary: Grinds Pouches, also knowns as Grinds Coffee Pouches or simply Grinds is a brand of caffeine pouches advertised as a healthy alternative to chewing tobacco. The company was founded in 2009 by Matt Canepa and Pat Pezet, making it one of the first caffeine pouches, nearly a decade before they rose to popularity in the mid-2020s. The original Grinds pouches were made with coffee grounds, but the company has also made energy and focus pouches with natural plant fibers, similar to other caffeine pouches currently on the market. Grinds was founded in California, and they are currently headquartered in Indiana.

rows.title: Hazen, New Hampshire
rows.description: Village in Whitefield, New Hampshire
rows.summary: Hazen or Hazens is a small village and farming community in Whitefield, New Hampshire. It was settled by Louis and Lucius Hazen in the 1870s. In 1887, the Grafton and Coos County Grange Fair came to the Hazen area.

rows.title: Herbert Blomstedt
rows.description: Swedish conductor (1927–2026)
rows.summary: Herbert Thorson Blomstedt was a Swedish and American conductor. Over the course of his 70-year career, he served as the principal conductor of orchestras, first in Scandinavia, where his first post was from 1954 with the Norrköping Symphony Orchestra, followed by tenures with the Oslo Philharmonic Orchestra, the Danish National Symphony Orchestra, and the Swedish Radio Symphony Orchestra. When he became principal conductor of the Staatskapelle Dresden in 1975, he was recognised internationally, and later led the San Francisco Symphony, the North German Radio Symphony Orchestra, and the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra. He conducted his last concert in May 2026, at age 98.

rows.title: History of Africa
rows.summary: Archaic humans emerged out of Africa between 0.5 and 1.8 million years ago. This was followed by the emergence of modern humans in East Africa around 300,000–250,000 years ago who spread across the world. The oral word is revered in most African cultures, and history has predominantly been passed down through oral tradition. In the 4th and 3rd millennia BCE Ancient Egypt and Kerma arose in the northeast, while the Tichitt Tradition flourished in West Africa. Between around 3000 BCE and 500 CE, the Bantu expansion swept from north-western Central Africa across much of Central, Eastern, and Southern Africa, displacing or absorbing groups such as the Khoisan and Pygmies.

rows.title: History of photography
rows.summary: The history of photography began with the discovery of two critical principles: The first is camera obscura image projection; the second is the discovery that some substances are visibly altered by exposure to light. There are no artifacts or descriptions that indicate any attempt to capture images with light-sensitive materials prior to the 18th century.

rows.title: Homerton University Hospital
rows.description: Hospital in Homerton, London
rows.summary: Homerton University Hospital is a teaching hospital in Homerton in the London Borough of Hackney. It is managed by Homerton Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust.

rows.title: Hubert Aiwanger
rows.description: German politician (1971–2026)
rows.summary: Hubert Aiwanger was a German politician. He was the party leader of the Free Voters from 2018 to 2026, the Deputy Minister-President of Bavaria and Bavarian Minister of Economic Affairs, Regional Development and Energy.

rows.title: Hyderabad International Convention Centre
rows.description: Venue in Hyderabad, Telangana, India
rows.summary:
Hyderabad International Convention Centre  is an modern Convention centre located in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. To create an events destination in Hyderabad, then chief minister N. Chandrababu Naidu created a convention hub with the Hyderabad International Convention Centre, is a purpose-built, state-of-the-art convention facility, the first of its kind in South Asia. The convention centre was built by Emaar MGF of India. It has been the winner of the excellence award for "Best Standalone Convention Centre" for a record four times, nationally awarded by Ministry of Tourism, Government of India and the company is part owned by Emaar of UAE. The facility is managed by Accor Hospitality.
The Hyderabad International Convention Centre with 5,000 seating capacity is India's largest convention facility. It is an integrated 27,000-square-metre (290,000 sq ft) covering 6.1 ha. The centre can be configured to increase seating capacity to about 6,500. The convention centre is connected to Novotel Hyderabad, an international business hotel, it has 288 rooms and is equipped with meeting rooms, restaurants, business centre, spa and a health club.

rows.title: Ian Millar
rows.description: Canadian equestrian
rows.summary: Ian Millar CM is a Canadian Equestrian Team athlete for show jumping. He is a two-time winner of the Show Jumping World Cup, and an Olympic silver medallist. Due to his longevity and accomplishments, he is often nicknamed "Captain Canada." He holds the record for most Olympic appearances by any athlete in any sport (10), shared with Georgian shooter Nino Salukvadze. A member of Canada's 2012 Olympic Games team, he broke the record when he took part in his tenth Games in London 2012.

rows.title: Ida Tarbell
rows.description: American writer, journalist, biographer and lecturer (1857–1944)
rows.summary: Ida Minerva Tarbell was an American writer, investigative journalist, biographer, and lecturer. She was one of the leading muckrakers and reformers of the Progressive Era of the late 19th and early 20th centuries and was a pioneer of investigative journalism.

rows.title: Influence of the French Revolution
rows.description: Impact of 1789–1799 sociopolitical change
rows.summary: The French Revolution had a major impact on Europe and the New World. Historians widely regard the Revolution as one of the most important events in European history. In the short-term, France lost thousands of its countrymen in the form of émigrés, or emigrants who wished to escape political tensions and save their lives. A number of individuals settled in the neighboring countries, while some settled in Russia, and many also went to Canada and the United States. The displacement of these Frenchmen led to a spread of French culture, policies regulating immigration, and a safe haven for Royalists and other counterrevolutionaries to outlast the violence of the French Revolution. The long-term impact on France was profound, shaping politics, society, religion and ideas for more than a century. The closer other countries were, the greater and deeper was the French impact, bringing liberalism, but also practices such as direct democracy and revolutionary terror along with the end of many feudal or traditional laws and practices. However, there was also a conservative counter-reaction that defeated Napoleon, reinstalled the Bourbon kings, and in some ways reversed the new reforms.

rows.title: It Was a Very Good Year
rows.description: 1961 song by Ervin Drake
rows.summary: "It Was a Very Good Year" is a song composed by Ervin Drake in 1961 and originally recorded by Bob Shane of the Kingston Trio for their album Goin' Places. It was made famous by Frank Sinatra's version in D minor from his album September of my Years, which won the Grammy Award for Best Male Vocal Performance at the 8th Annual Grammy Awards in 1966 and became Sinatra's first number one Adult Contemporary single, also peaking at No. 28 on the Billboard Hot 100. Gordon Jenkins won a Grammy Award for his arrangement for the orchestra, which he also conducted.

rows.title: J. J. Walsh
rows.description: Irish politician (1880–1948)
rows.summary: James Joseph Walsh was an Irish politician who served as Postmaster General, of the Irish Free State from 1923 to 1927. He was also a senior Gaelic Athletic Association organiser and Cumann na nGaedheal politician. Later, Walsh had heavy connections with fascism, including his association with Ailtirí na hAiséirghe.

rows.title: Jake Humphrey
rows.description: English television presenter and entrepreneur
rows.summary: Jacob John Humphrey is an English broadcaster, author and entrepreneur. He is best known for hosting BBC Sport's coverage of Formula One, presenting football coverage for BT Sport, and for his work as co-founder of the television production company Whisper Group.

rows.title: James Woods
rows.description: American actor (born 1947)
rows.summary: James Howard Woods is an American actor. Known for fast-talking, intense roles on screen and stage, he has received numerous accolades, including three Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe Award, as well as nominations for two Academy Awards and three Actor Awards. Woods made his Broadway debut in the Elliott Baker play The Penny Wars (1969). His early films roles include The Visitors (1972), The Way We Were (1973) and The Gambler (1974), before starring with Meryl Streep in the NBC miniseries Holocaust (1978).

rows.title: Jan Byś
rows.description: Polish footballer (1953–2026)
rows.summary: Jan Byś was a Polish footballer who played as a midfielder. He was a key part of the Szombierki Bytom squad that won the 1980 Ekstraklasa title. The following season, he scored the club's first European home goal.

rows.title: Jason Voorhees
rows.description: Friday the 13th antagonist
rows.summary: Jason Voorhees is a fictional character and the antagonist of the Friday the 13th franchise. He first appeared in Friday the 13th (1980) as the young son of camp-cook-turned-killer Pamela Voorhees, in which he was portrayed by Ari Lehman. Created by Victor Miller, with contributions by Ron Kurz, Sean S. Cunningham and Tom Savini, Jason was not originally intended to carry the series as the main antagonist. The character has subsequently been represented in various other media, including novels, video games, and comic books.

rows.title: Jay B. Silveria
rows.description: US Air Force lieutenant general
rows.summary: Jay Benton Silveria is a retired lieutenant general in the United States Air Force who has served as president of the University of Arkansas System since 2025. He previously served as superintendent of the Air Force Academy from 2017 to 2020. His previous commands include deputy commander of the United States Air Forces Central Command, commander of the United States Air Force Warfare Center, and commander of 48th Fighter Wing. Rated as a command pilot, Silvera has more than 3,900 flying hours.

rows.title: Jean Talon
rows.description: Colonial administrator of New France (1626–1694)
rows.summary: Jean Talon, Count d'Orsainville was a French colonial administrator who served as the first Intendant of New France. Talon was appointed by King Louis XIV and his minister, Jean-Baptiste Colbert, to serve as the Intendant of Justice, Public Order and Finances in Canada, Acadia and Newfoundland for two terms: 1665 to 1668 and 1670 to 1672.

rows.summary: Kilkis is a city in Central Macedonia, Greece. As of 2021, there were 24,130 people living in the city proper, 27,493 people living in the municipal unit, and 45,308 in the municipality of Kilkis. It is also the capital city of the regional unit of Kilkis.

rows.title: Kimmarie Johnson
rows.description: American model and businesswoman (1976–2026)
rows.summary: Kimmarie Johnson was an American actress, model, businesswoman and beauty pageant titleholder. She was the founder of SkinGlow by Kimmarie, a skin care and beauty retailing and consulting company she founded in 2011.

rows.title: King Simmons
rows.description: American football player (born 1963)
rows.summary: King David Simmons is an American former professional football player who was a defensive back for the San Diego Chargers of the National Football League (NFL). rows.description: Kenyan politician

He is also a former advisor to President Mwai Kibaki. Prof. Kibwana's second term as the first Governor of Makueni County ended in 2022.

rows.title: Kowloon Walled City
rows.description: Former slum in Hong Kong
rows.summary: Kowloon Walled City was an ungoverned and densely populated de jure Chinese enclave within the boundaries of British Hong Kong. Originally the site of a military fort, it became an enclave after the New Territories were leased to Britain in 1898. The Walled City's population increased dramatically following World War II, and by 1987 it had an estimated 33,000 residents within its 2.6-hectare borders, making it one of the most densely populated places on Earth at approximately 1.2 million inhabitants per square kilometre. The city was demolished between 1993 and 1994; the Kowloon Walled City Park was built in its place and opened in December 1995.

rows.summary: In 2015, Condé Nast Traveler described Beijing's LGBTQ scene as "under-the-radar yet energized". rows.title: Lew Sapieha
rows.description: Polish–Lithuanian nobleman (1557–1633)

rows.title: Long division

rows.summary: In arithmetic, long division is a standard division algorithm suitable for dividing multi-digit numbers that is simple enough to perform by hand. It breaks down a division problem into a series of easier steps.

rows.title: Madonna of the Pinks
rows.description: Painting by Raphael
rows.summary: The Madonna of the Pinks is an early devotional painting usually attributed to Italian Renaissance master Raphael. It is painted in oils on yew [Taxus baccata] wood, a first for a Raphael or any currently known Italian Renaissance painting, and now hangs in the National Gallery in London.

rows.title: Mariposa Food Co-op
rows.description: Food cooperative in Philadelphia
rows.summary: Mariposa Food Co-op is a food cooperative located in West Philadelphia. Founded in 1971, Mariposa is a consumer cooperative that sells groceries and other products. The store began as a buyers club, and later expanded to a storefront operated by its owner members. It currently operates out of a former bank building on Baltimore Avenue, and is open to the public.

rows.title: Matthew James-Bailey
rows.description: English actor (born 1995)
rows.summary: Matthew James-Bailey is an English actor. He is most known for portraying the role of Ethan Williams in the Channel 4 soap opera Hollyoaks (2021–2024). He played the role of DC Craig Ingram in the BBC soap EastEnders in 2026, departing the show in the episode broadcast 5 November.

rows.title: Max Cullen
rows.description: Australian-born stage and screen actor (born 1940)
rows.summary: Maxwell Phillip Cullen is an Australian stage and screen character actor. He has appeared in many Australian films, television series and theatre productions, he is perhaps best known for his role in the film Spider and Rose and the television series The Flying Doctors, Secret Valley and Love My Way.

rows.title: Men's Asian Champions Trophy
rows.description: Field hockey championship
rows.summary: The Men's Asian Champions Trophy is an event held annually by the Asian Hockey Federation since 2011. It features Asia's six top field hockey teams in the hockey season competing in a round robin format. India is the most successful team in the tournament history, winning the trophy six times. The next most frequent champion has been Pakistan, winning the trophy thrice.

rows.title: Michael Saward (political theorist)
rows.summary: Michael Saward, is an Australian and British political theorist and professor emeritus of politics and international studies at the University of Warwick, He was formerly reader in politics at Royal Holloway, University of London, professor and head of department in politics and international studies at the Open University,and professor of politics and international studies at the University of Warwick.

rows.title: Microsoft Paint
rows.description: Raster graphics editor
rows.summary: Microsoft Paint is a simple raster graphics editor that has been included with all versions of Microsoft Windows. The program opens, modifies, and saves image files in Windows bitmap (BMP), JPEG, GIF, PNG, and single-page TIFF formats. The program can be in color mode or two-color black-and-white, but there is no grayscale mode. For its simplicity and wide availability, it rapidly became one of the most used Windows applications, introducing many to painting on a computer for the first time.

rows.title: Military budget of the Soviet Union
rows.description: Military expenditure of the USSR
rows.summary: The military budget of the Soviet Union was the portion of the military budget the portion of the overall budget of the USSR government that was allocated for the funding of the Soviet Armed Forces. This military budget financed employee salaries and training costs, the maintenance of equipment and facilities, support of operations, and development and procurement of weapons, equipment, and vehicles. Particularly during the Cold War the level of military spending of the USSR was a matter of dispute and research, since the USSR did not publish reliable figures for its military expenditure. The burden of its military expenditure is believed to have been amongst factors contributing to the fall of the Soviet Union.

rows.title: Miracle of the Sun
rows.description: Purported miracle in 1917
rows.summary: The Miracle of the Sun, also known as the Miracle of Fátima, is a series of events reported to have occurred miraculously on 13 October 1917, attended by a large crowd in the tens of thousands who had gathered in Fátima, Portugal, in response to a prophecy made by three shepherd children, Lúcia Santos and Francisco and Jacinta Marto. The prophecy was that the Virgin Mary would appear and perform miracles on that date. Newspapers published testimony from witnesses who said that they had seen extraordinary solar activity, such as the Sun appearing to "dance" or zig-zag in the sky, advance towards the Earth, or emit multicolored light and radiant colors. According to these reports, the event lasted approximately ten minutes.

rows.title: Mizanur Rahman Azhari
rows.description: Bangladeshi Islamic preacher and author (born 1990)
rows.summary: Mizanur Rahman Azhari is a Bangladeshi Islamic preacher and author. He is known for his public lectures on the Quran and hadith, particularly at waz mahfil gatherings, and for the circulation of his recorded sermons online. He studied at Al-Azhar University in Egypt and International Islamic University Malaysia.

rows.title: Mohammad Ibrahim (footballer, born 1997)
rows.description: Bangladeshi footballer
rows.summary: Mohammad Ibrahim is a Bangladeshi professional footballer who plays as a winger for Bangladesh Football League club Fortis and the Bangladesh national team.

rows.title: Mokhzani Mahathir
rows.description: Malaysian businessman and motorsports administrator
rows.summary: Tan Sri Mokhzani bin Mahathir is a Malaysian businessman and motorsports administrator. A petroleum engineer by training, he began his career with Sarawak Shell Berhad before holding senior positions in Tongkah Holdings Berhad and Pantai Holdings Berhad. He later became involved in the oil and gas industry through Kencana Petroleum, which was listed in 2006 and merged with SapuraCrest Petroleum in 2012 to form SapuraKencana Petroleum.

rows.title: Moses Harris
