rows.summary: Moses Harris was an English entomologist and engraver.

rows.title: Myers–Briggs Type Indicator
rows.description: Pseudoscientific personality questionnaire
rows.summary: The Myers–Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) is a self-report questionnaire that makes pseudoscientific claims to categorize individuals into 16 distinct psychological types. The test assigns a binary letter value to each of four dichotomous categories: introversion or extraversion, sensing or intuition, thinking or feeling, and judging or perceiving. This produces a four-letter test result, such as "INTJ" or "ESFP", representing one of the 16 types.

rows.title: Nefertari
rows.description: Wife of the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses II
rows.summary: Nefertari was an Egyptian queen and the first of the Great Royal Wives of Ramesses the Great. She is one of the best known Egyptian queens, among such women as Cleopatra, Nefertiti, and Hatshepsut, and one of the most prominent Egyptian royal consorts. She was highly educated and able to both read and write hieroglyphs, a very rare skill at the time. She used these skills in her diplomatic work, corresponding with other prominent royals of the time. Her lavishly decorated tomb, QV66, is one of the largest and most spectacular in the Valley of the Queens. Ramesses also constructed a temple for her at Abu Simbel next to his colossal monument there.

rows.title: Neha Bora
rows.description: Indian student activist (born 1997)
rows.summary: Neha Bora is an Indian activist and PhD student. They are the national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA) and an active participant in India's Gen-Z movements.

rows.title: New Caledonia national football team
rows.summary: The New Caledonia men's national football team, nicknamed Les Cagous, is the national team of New Caledonia; it is controlled by the Fédération Calédonienne de Football. Although they were only admitted to FIFA in 2004, they have been participating in the OFC Nations Cup since its inception. They have been one of this relatively small region's strongest teams, finishing second in 2008 and 2012, and third in 1973 and 1980. They were the top ranked OFC nation at number 95 in September 2008, making them only the fourth country from the confederation to have reached the global top 100.

rows.title: Newhart
rows.description: American television sitcom (1982–1990)
rows.summary: Newhart is an American television sitcom that aired on CBS from October 25, 1982, to May 21, 1990, with a total of 184 half-hour episodes produced for eight seasons. This was Bob Newhart's third show, and it was his second for CBS. Newhart's co-star Suzanne Pleshette did not return to the show until the series finale, the misadventures of an author turned innkeeper in rural Vermont and his friends, as Dick and Joanna Loudon run the fictitious Stratford Inn. TV Guide, TV Land, and A&E named the Newhart series finale as one of the most memorable in television history. The theme music for Newhart was composed by Henry Mancini.

rows.title: Nic Cravillion
rows.description: American politician
rows.summary: Nicolas William "Nic" Cravillion is an American small business owner and Republican politician from Brown County, Wisconsin. He is a member-elect of the Wisconsin Senate, and will represent Wisconsin's 1st Senate district in the 108th Wisconsin Legislature (2027–2028). He previously worked as district director for his predecessor in this state Senate seat, André Jacque, and before that he served in a similar capacity for state senator Roger Roth.

rows.title: Ninja lanternshark
rows.description: Species of shark
rows.summary: The ninja lanternshark is of the family Etmopteridae, found in the eastern Pacific Ocean from Nicaragua, south to Panama and Costa Rica. The depth range of collections is from 836 to 1443 meters along the continental slope. E. benchleyi is the only Etmopterus species presently known from the Pacific Coast of Central America.

rows.title: Nithya Raman
rows.description: American politician (born 1981)
rows.summary: Nithya Varsha Raman is an American politician and urban planner who is the mayor-elect of Los Angeles. A member of the Democratic Party and the Democratic Socialists of America, Raman has served as the Los Angeles city councilmember for the 4th district since 2020.

rows.title: Nottingham New Theatre
rows.description: Theatre on University Park Campus, Nottingham, England
rows.summary: The Nottingham New Theatre was formerly a playhouse on the University Park Campus, Nottingham, England, which closed in 2023. It was the only entirely student-run theatre in England.

rows.title: Opinion polling for the 2026 New Zealand general election
rows.summary: Eight polling firms have conducted opinion polls during the term of the 54th New Zealand Parliament (2023–2026) for the 2026 New Zealand general election. The regular polls are the quarterly polls produced by Television New Zealand, conducted by Verian, Radio New Zealand (RNZ), conducted by Reid Research, and The Post, conducted by Freshwater Strategy, along with monthly polls by Roy Morgan and by Curia. Curia Market Research is no longer a member of the Research Association of New Zealand, following complaints and the resignation from RANZ by its principal, David Farrar. The sample size, margin of error, and confidence interval of each poll varies by organisation and date. The parliament was elected on 14 October 2023, and the election is scheduled to be held on 7 November 2026.

rows.title: Osmotic power
rows.description: Sustainable energy from sea and river water
rows.summary:
Osmotic power, salinity gradient power or blue energy is the energy available from the difference in the salt concentration between seawater and river water. Two practical methods for this are reverse electrodialysis (RED) and
pressure retarded osmosis (PRO). Both processes rely on osmosis with membranes. The key waste product is brackish water. This byproduct is the result of natural forces that are being harnessed: the flow of fresh water into seas that are made up of salt water.

rows.title: Owen Oyston
rows.description: English businessman and rapist (born 1934)
rows.summary: John Owen Oyston is an English businessman best known as the former majority owner of Blackpool Football Club. Oyston was convicted of rape and indecent assault of a 16-year-old girl in 1996. He served three years and six months of a six-year sentence in prison. He was released after a judicial review of the parole board's refusal to grant parole. On 25 February 2019, Oyston and his daughter, Natalie Christopher, were removed from the board of Blackpool Football Club.

rows.title: P. G. T. Beauregard
rows.description: Confederate States Army general (1818–1893)
rows.summary: Pierre Gustave Toutant-Beauregard was an American military officer known for being the Confederate general who started the American Civil War at the Battle of Fort Sumter on April 12, 1861. Today, he is commonly referred to as P. G. T. Beauregard, but he rarely used his first name as an adult. He signed correspondence as G. T. Beauregard.

rows.title: Paul Scott (footballer, born 1979)
rows.description: English footballer
rows.summary: Paul Scott is an English former professional footballer who played in the Football League with Huddersfield Town, Bury and Morecambe.

rows.title: Pedro Alliana
rows.description: President of Paraguay since 2026
rows.summary: Hércules Pedro Lorenzo Alliana Rodríguez is a Paraguayan politician who serves as the President of the Republic of Paraguay since 6 November 2026. A former National Deputy of Paraguay from 2013 to 2023, he previously served as president of the Chamber of Deputies of Paraguay from 2019 to 2022, president of the Colorado Party from 2015 to 2023, and governor of the Ñeembucú department from 2008 to 2013.

rows.title: Polonium
rows.description: Chemical element with atomic number 84 (Po)
rows.summary: Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84. A rare and highly radioactive metal with no stable isotopes, polonium is a chalcogen and chemically similar to selenium and tellurium, though its metallic character resembles that of its horizontal neighbours in the periodic table: thallium, lead, and bismuth. Due to the short half-life of all its isotopes, its natural occurrence is limited to tiny traces of the fleeting polonium-210 in uranium ores, as it is the penultimate daughter of natural uranium-238. Though two longer-lived isotopes exist, they are much more difficult to produce. Today, polonium is usually produced in milligram quantities by the neutron irradiation of bismuth. Due to its intense radioactivity, which results in the radiolysis of chemical bonds and radioactive self-heating, its chemistry has mostly been investigated on the trace scale only.

rows.title: Prime Marina
rows.description: Marina-front residential development in Colombo, Sri Lanka
rows.summary: Prime Marina is a luxury marina-front residential development located within the Marina District of the Port City Colombo in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

rows.title: Princess Jalila of Hejaz
rows.description: Hijazi princess
rows.summary: Princess Jalila of Hejaz was a Hijazi princess. She was the daughter of Ali, King of Hejaz and Princess Nafeesa. Her elder sister was Aliya, Queen of Iraq, wife of King Ghazi of Iraq and mother of King Faisal II of Iraq. Her brother was Abdullah, regent and crown prince of Iraq.

rows.title: Protests against Donald Trump
rows.description: Worldwide demonstrations since 2015
rows.summary: Protests against Donald Trump have occurred in the United States and internationally, mostly after his entry into the 2016 presidential campaign. Protests have expressed opposition to Trump's campaign rhetoric, his ideology, his electoral win, his first inauguration, his alleged history of sexual misconduct, including a 2023 verdict in which he was held liable for sexual abuse, and various presidential actions, including his travel ban in 2017 and aggressive family separation policy in 2018.

rows.title: Puy de Sarran
rows.description: Mountain in France
rows.summary: The Puy de Sarran is a summit of the Massif Central in France. At an altitude of 819m, it is located in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region, in the Corrèze department, in the Massif des Monédières.

rows.title: Ramayana: Part 1
rows.description: 2026 Indian film by Nitesh Tiwari
rows.summary: Ramayana: Part 1 is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language epic mythological film directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film is based on the epic poem Ramayana by Valmiki. It is the first of a two-part film, with Part 1 being based on the first three kāṇḍa (chapters) of Ramayana which chronicles the life of Prince Rama from childhood up to his adventurous 14-year exile. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Sunny Deol, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta.

rows.title: Ratatoskr
rows.description: Norse mythical animal
rows.summary: In Norse mythology, Ratatoskr is a squirrel who runs up and down the world tree Yggdrasil to carry messages between the eagles perched atop it and the dragon Níðhöggr who dwells beneath one of the three roots of the tree. Ratatoskr is attested in the Poetic Edda, compiled in the 13th century from earlier traditional sources, and the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson.

rows.title: Richard Allen Davis
rows.description: American murderer
rows.summary: Richard Allen Davis is an American convicted murderer whose criminal record fueled support for the passage of California's "three-strikes law" for repeat offenders and the involuntary civil commitment act for sex offenders and predators. He was convicted in 1996 of first-degree murder with special circumstances of 12-year-old Polly Klaas.

rows.title: Riva Taylor
rows.description: British singer
rows.summary: Rebecca Jane Grosvenor Taylor, known professionally as Riva Taylor, is an English singer and actress. In her childhood and teens, she recorded under the names Becky Taylor, Becky Jane Taylor, and simply Becky.

rows.title: RoadBlasters
rows.description: 1987 video game
rows.summary: RoadBlasters is a 1987 vehicular combat video game developed and published by Atari Games for arcades. The player navigates an armed sports car through 50 different rally races, getting to the finish line before running out of fuel. Ports were released for a variety of home systems by Tengen and U.S. Gold.

rows.title: Rob Beckett
rows.description: English comedian (born 1986)
rows.summary: Robert Anthony Beckett is an English comedian, actor, and presenter. He was a co-host on the ITV2 spin-off show I'm a Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here! NOW! from 2012 to 2014, and a team captain on the E4 panel show 8 Out of 10 Cats from 2016 to 2021. Since 2025, Beckett has been a team captain on the Channel 4 panel show 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown and the narrator of the reality series Celebs Go Dating since 2016. He presented BBC One entertainment series Wedding Day Winners and All Together Now.

rows.title: Robert Atkins (physician)
rows.description: American physician (1930–2003)
rows.summary: Robert Coleman Atkins was an American physician and cardiologist, best known for the Atkins Diet, which requires close control of carbohydrate consumption and emphasizes protein and fat as the primary sources of dietary calories in addition to a controlled number of carbohydrates from vegetables.

rows.title: Rolijah Hardy
rows.description: American football player (born 2004)
rows.summary: Rolijah Hardy is an American football linebacker for the Indiana Hoosiers. He previously played for the Navy Midshipmen.

rows.title: Royal Bermuda Regiment
rows.description: Infantry regiment of the British Army
rows.summary: The Royal Bermuda Regiment (RBR) is a reserve regiment of the British Army, tasked as the home defence unit of the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda. It is a single territorial infantry battalion that was formed on the amalgamation in 1965 of two originally voluntary units, the mostly black Bermuda Militia Artillery (BMA) and the almost entirely white Bermuda Rifles, and the only remaining component of the Bermuda Garrison since the 1957 withdrawal of regular units and detachments from Bermuda.

rows.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK series 8
rows.description: 2026 series of RuPaul's Drag Race UK
rows.summary: The eighth series of RuPaul's Drag Race UK premiered on BBC Three on 3 September 2026. RuPaul returned as the main host and head judge, with Michelle Visage, Alan Carr and Graham Norton forming the judging panel. The series began filming in January 2026.

rows.title: Russell Brand
rows.description: English comedian and actor (born 1975)
rows.summary: Russell Edward Brand is an English comedian, actor and media personality. He rose to prominence as the host of Big Brother's Big Mouth, a spin-off of the reality television series Big Brother broadcast on E4. He had his first major film role in the British comedy St Trinian's (2007), after which he starred in the Hollywood comedies Forgetting Sarah Marshall (2008), Get Him to the Greek (2010), Arthur (2011), and Rock of Ages (2012), as well as the mystery film Death on the Nile (2022). He has also voiced roles in the Despicable Me franchise (2010–2022), Hop (2011), Trolls (2016), and Under the Boardwalk (2023). Additionally, he has released several stand-up specials, including Scandalous (2009), Messiah Complex (2013), and Brandemic (2023). He hosted his own radio show The Russell Brand Show and has hosted the podcasts Stay Free with Russell Brand and Under the Skin with Russell Brand. He has received three British Comedy Awards and a nomination for a BAFTA Award.

rows.title: Russell Brands
rows.description: American corporation
rows.summary: Russell Brands, LLC was an American corporation that manufactured sports equipment, marketing its products under many brands and subsidiaries, such as Russell Athletic and Spalding. Formerly a publicly traded company, Russell Brands was acquired by Fruit of the Loom, a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway, in 2006.

rows.title: Saif Ali Khan
rows.description: Indian actor and film producer (born 1970)
rows.summary: Saif Ali Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi is an Indian actor and film producer who primarily works in Hindi films. The titular head of the Pataudi family since 2011, he is the son of actress Sharmila Tagore and cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi. Khan has won several awards, including a National Film Award and seven Filmfare Awards, and received the Padma Shri, the fourth highest Indian civilian award in 2010.

rows.title: Saint Peter
rows.description: Apostle of Jesus
rows.summary: Saint Peter, also known as Peter the Apostle, Simon Peter, or Cephas, was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus and one of the first leaders of the early Christian Church. He appears repeatedly and prominently in all four New Testament gospels, as well as the Acts of the Apostles. Catholic and Orthodox tradition treats Peter as the first bishop of Rome and also as the first bishop of Antioch. According to Christian tradition, Peter was crucified upside down in Rome under Emperor Nero.

rows.title: Salem Poor
rows.description: African-American Revolutionary War soldier (1747–1802)
rows.summary: Salem Poor was an enslaved African-American man who purchased his freedom in 1769 and became a soldier in 1775. He was involved in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the Battle of Bunker Hill.

rows.title: Salon (website)
rows.description: American progressive news and opinion website
rows.summary: Salon was an American politically progressive news and opinion website which ran from 1995 to 2026. It published articles on U.S. politics, culture, and current events.

rows.title: Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
rows.description: Ongoing military intervention
rows.summary: Since 21 October 2026, El Salvador has been conducting a military intervention in Haiti following a gang ambush on 18 October that resulted in four Salvadoran aviation technicians of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) being kidnapped. According to Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele, the intervention's primary objective is to rescue the four technicians, while threatening to "finish" the Haitian gangs if the technicians are not rescued alive.

rows.title: Samuel de Champlain
rows.description: French explorer of North America (1574–1635)
rows.summary: Samuel de Champlain was a French explorer, navigator, cartographer, soldier, geographer, diplomat, and chronicler who founded Quebec City and established New France as a permanent French colony in North America.

rows.title: Santiago Peña
rows.description: President of Paraguay from 2023 to 2026
rows.summary: Santiago Peña Palacios is a Paraguayan politician and economist who served as the 52nd president of Paraguay from 2023 until his dismissal in 2026. Peña served on leadership boards for the Central Bank of Paraguay and Banco Amambay. He taught economics at the Catholic University of Asunción.

rows.title: Scene (2026 film)
rows.description: 2026 Indian film by Jithu Madhavan
rows.summary: Scene is a 2026 Indian Tamil-language action comedy film written and directed by Jithu Madhavan. Produced by Suriya and Jyothika's 2D Entertainment and the newly established Zhagaram Studios, the film stars Suriya, Naslen and Nazriya Nazim. It revolves around a police officer being forced to reopen an unfinished case and solve it with a troublesome team.

rows.title: Scott Colom
rows.description: American lawyer (born 1982)
rows.summary: Scott Winston Colom is an American lawyer and politician serving since 2016 as district attorney for the 16th Judicial District of Mississippi. He is the Democratic nominee in the 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi.

rows.title: Senate of the Dominican Republic
rows.description: Upper house in the legislature of the Dominican Republic
rows.summary: The Senate of the Dominican Republic is the upper house in the bicameral legislature of the Dominican Republic, and together with the Chamber of Deputies makes up the Congress.

rows.title: Showboy
rows.description: 2002 American film
rows.summary: Showboy is a 2002 mockumentary film that was produced by Jason Buchtel, directed by Christian Taylor and Lindy Heymann, and written by and starring the three. It has cameos by Whoopi Goldberg, Siegfried & Roy, Alan Ball and the cast of the television series Six Feet Under.

rows.title: Simran filmography
rows.description: Filmography article
rows.summary: Simran is an Indian actress and film producer known for her works in Tamil and Telugu films. She has also appeared in Hindi, Malayalam and Kannada films. She is well noted for her dancing and acting skills in the Indian film industry. After her marriage, Simran took a break from acting in films and moved on to the small screen where she acted in Jaya TV's serial Simran Thirai, which consisted of mini-serials all featuring Simran and included many popular stars such as Ramji, Raaghav, Saakshi Siva and Abitha playing supporting roles. In 2009, she started acting in the Telugu serial Sundarakanda, telecast on Gemini TV, where she did a guest role. The serial was dubbed in Tamil as Sundarakandam and telecast on Polimer TV. In 2012, she hosted Jackpot, a game show on Jaya TV which was earlier hosted by Khushbu and Nadhiya. She acted in Agni Paravai, a serial telecast in Puthuyugam TV. She played as a main judge on the reality show Dance Tamizha Dance, which was produced by her and her husband Mr Deepak Bagga for Zee Tamizh.

rows.title: Skateboarding at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics – Women's street
rows.summary: The women's street competition at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics took place on 5 November at the Complexe Tour de l'Oeuf in Dakar, Senegal.

rows.title: Softball
rows.description: Team ball sport
rows.summary: Softball is a bat-and-ball sport played between two teams on a diamond-shaped field, who take turns batting and fielding. There are two primary forms: Fast-pitch and slow-pitch. In both forms, the pitcher throws the ball underhand to batters. In fast-pitch, the ball is typically thrown with a "windmill" motion and releasing the ball at hip level. Pitchers throw balls up to 78 miles per hour (124 km/h). Fast-pitch is played at the high school, collegiate, and professional levels. Women's fast-pitch softball was introduced to the Summer Olympic Games in 1996. Softball was not included in the 2024 Summer Olympics but will return for the 2028 Summer Olympics. Slow-pitch softball is commonly played in recreational leagues, with the ball being pitched at slow speeds and slightly simplified rules, making it an accessible sport for people of many ages.

rows.title: Sonority sequencing principle
rows.description: Phonological principle observed in many languages
rows.summary: The sonority sequencing principle (SSP), or sonority sequencing constraint, is a phonotactic principle that aims to explain or predict the structure of a syllable in terms of sonority.

rows.title: Steve Lyon (producer)
rows.description: British music producer
rows.summary: Steve Lyon is a British record producer, recording and mixing engineer known for his work with Depeche Mode and The Cure.

rows.title: Streptococcus bovis
rows.description: Species of bacterium
rows.summary: Streptococcus bovis is a historical name applied to bacteria subsequently classified into several species and subspecies within the Streptococcus bovis/Streptococcus equinus complex, or SBSEC. The eight members of this complex are closely related Gram-positive bacteria.

rows.title: Swan Valley, Idaho
rows.description: City in Idaho, United States
rows.summary: Swan Valley is a city in Bonneville County, Idaho, United States. It is part of the Idaho Falls, Idaho Metropolitan Statistical Area. The population was 225 at the 2020 census.

rows.title: Swarnim Wagle
rows.description: Nepalese Minister of Finance since 2026
rows.summary: Dr. Swarnim Wagle is a Nepalese politician and prominent South Asian economist who has served as the Minister of Finance since 2026. He is also the vice-chairperson of the Rastriya Swatantra Party. He was formerly a chief economic advisor at the UNDP Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific (RBAP) in New York.

rows.title: Tado (comedian)
rows.description: Filipino actor and comedian (1974–2014)
rows.summary: Arvin Impuesto Jimenez, known mononymously as Tado, was a Filipino comedian, actor, radio personality, businessman, published author and activist. His nickname "Tado" comes from a Tagalog expletive (tarantado) that he frequently blurts out. Tado was primarily known for the offbeat television program Strangebrew and the U92 radio program The BrewRATs!.

rows.title: Tater tots
rows.description: Deep-fried grated potato cylinders
rows.summary: Tater tots are grated potato formed into small cylinders and deep-fried, often served as a side dish. "Tater" is a dialect form of the word potato. The name "tater tot" is a registered trademark of the American frozen food company Ore-Ida, but is often used as a generic term. Ore-Ida also markets a coin-shaped version called "Crispy Crowns".

rows.title: Taurotragus
rows.description: Subgenus of mammals
rows.summary: Taurotragus is a subgenus of genus Tragelaphus. This subgenus consists of giant antelopes of the African savanna, commonly known as elands or impofu. This subgenus contains two species: the common eland Tragelaphus oryx and the giant eland Tragelaphus derbianus.

rows.title: Ted
rows.description: Topics referred to by the same term
rows.summary: Ted may refer to:

rows.title: Texas horned lizard
rows.description: Species of lizard
rows.summary: The Texas horned lizard is one of about 21 North American species of spikey-bodied reptiles called horned lizards, all belonging the genus Phrynosoma. It occurs in south-central regions of the US and northeastern Mexico, as well as several isolated introduced records and populations from Southern United States. Though some populations are stable, severe population declines have occurred in many areas of Texas and Oklahoma. The Texas spiny lizard may be confused for a Texas horned lizard due to its appearance and overlapping habitat. Texas horned lizard populations show strong genetic structuring across their range, with limited gene flow between regions. Because the Texas horned lizard is listed as a threatened species in the state, it is illegal to pick up, touch, or possess them in Texas.

rows.title: The Cat in the Hat (2026 film)
rows.description: Animated film by Warner Bros.
rows.summary: The Cat in the Hat is a 2026 American animated fantasy comedy film loosely based on the 1957 children's book by Dr. Seuss. Written and directed by Alessandro Carloni and Erica Rivinoja, it is the second feature-length adaptation of the book following the 2003 live-action film. Bill Hader stars as the voice of the titular character, alongside Matt Berry, Quinta Brunson, Xochitl Gomez, Giancarlo Esposito, and America Ferrera.

rows.title: The Finish Line (game show)
rows.description: UK TV quiz show
rows.summary: The Finish Line is a British game show that first aired on 21 August 2023, starring Roman Kemp as host and Sarah Greene as co-host. Five contestants compete in four rounds, each eliminating a contestant, with the one remaining contestant playing one final round in an attempt to win £5,000. The show sees these contestants answering quick-fire questions on moving podiums that are mounted on parallel lanes of a track, attempting to cross the finish line to remain in the game.

rows.title: The Four of Us (TV series)
rows.description: South African drama television series
rows.summary: The Four Of Us is a new telenovela produced by Tshedza Pictures airing on e.tv at 8PM weeknights with episodes streaming on Netflix the following day, it replaced long running soapie Scandal!.

rows.title: The Legislative War of 1893
rows.summary: The Legislative War of 1893 was an armed conflict that took place between the Populist Party and Republican Party in Topeka, Kansas, United States, at the Kansas State Capitol Building in 1893.

rows.title: The Wildworld Tour
rows.description: 2026 concert tour by Katseye
rows.summary: The Wildworld Tour is the second concert tour by girl group Katseye, held in support of their third extended play (EP), Wild (2026). The tour began on September 1, 2026, in Dublin, Ireland, and is currently set to conclude on March 6, 2027, in Auckland, New Zealand, spanning 43 shows across Europe, North America, Asia and Oceania. It is their first arena concert tour. Members Manon Bannerman and Sophia Laforteza did not participate in the European and American legs of the tour due to their respective hiatuses; Laforteza is set to return from her hiatus in January 2027.

rows.title: Tom Welling
rows.description: American actor, podcaster, director, and model (born 1977)
rows.summary: Thomas Joseph Welling is an American actor, director, and producer. He is best known for his role as Clark Kent/Kal El in The WB superhero drama Smallville (2001–2011). He also co-starred in the third season of the Fox fantasy comedy-drama Lucifer as Lt. Marcus Pierce/Cain (2017–2018).

rows.title: Ueno Bank
rows.description: Paraguayan bank
rows.summary: UENO Bank S.A., doing business as ueno bank, was a Paraguayan bank headquartered in Asunción. It operated primarily through digital payment platforms and originated from the consolidation of financial institutions with roots dating back to 1976. In November 2023, it obtained a banking license from the Central Bank of Paraguay, and in 2024 it absorbed Visión Banco, significantly expanding its customer base. By June 2026, it reported approximately 2.94 million customers. The institution also maintained sponsorship agreements with major Paraguayan sporting organizations, including the Paraguayan Football Association, as well as cultural and social initiatives.

rows.title: Ujjani Dam
rows.description: Dam in Indapur ,pune
rows.summary: Ujani Dam, also known as Bhima Dam or Bhima Irrigation Project, on the Bhima River, is an earthfill cum Masonry gravity dam located near Indapur of Pune District of the state of Maharashtra in India.

rows.title: United States midterm election
rows.description: General elections in the United States
rows.summary: Midterm elections in the United States are the general elections that are held near the midpoint of a president's four-year term of office, on Election Day on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November. Federal offices that are up for election during the midterms include all 435 seats in the United States House of Representatives, and 33 or 34 of the 100 seats in the United States Senate.

rows.title: Vessel (Twenty One Pilots album)
rows.description: 2013 studio album by Twenty One Pilots
rows.summary: Vessel is the third studio album by the American musical duo Twenty One Pilots, which was released on January 8, 2013. It is the band's first album released via Fueled by Ramen, and is their major-label debut album. Vessel debuted at number 58 on the Billboard 200 chart, but reached its peak at number 21 in 2016 following the duo's mainstream breakthrough. As of July 2019, the album has sold over two million equivalent album units in the U.S. All of its tracks have been certified at least Gold by the RIAA, which made Twenty One Pilots the first group or artist to achieve this feat with two separate albums. The album received positive reviews from critics.

rows.title: Vice President of Paraguay
rows.summary: The vice president of Paraguay is the person with the second highest position in the executive branch of the Paraguayan government, after the president of Paraguay. The position of vice president was created with the Constitution of 1844, although it was the title given to ex officio members temporarily replacing the elected president in case of death or absence, and was not a position elected alongside the president.

rows.title: Victoria Broderick
rows.description: American politician
rows.summary: Victoria Isabel Broderick is an American politician who is a member-elect of the United States House of Representatives for Tennessee's 4th congressional district. A member of the Democratic Party, she narrowly defeated Scott DesJarlais in the 2026 election in an upset.

rows.title: Violence and autism
rows.description: Sociocultural issue involving autism
rows.summary: A popular belief is that people who suffer from autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are more likely to be violent or commit crimes than those who are non-autistic. Separately, autistic people are more likely to be victims of bullying, abuse, and other violence themselves.

rows.title: VisionQuest
rows.description: Marvel Studios television miniseries
rows.summary: VisionQuest is an American television miniseries created by Terry Matalas for the streaming service Disney+, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Vision. A spin-off from and sequel to the miniseries WandaVision (2021), it is the 18th television series in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) from Marvel Studios and is produced under its Marvel Television label. The series shares continuity with the films of the MCU. It follows the synthezoid Vision as he attempts to understand who he is by communicating with AI personas embedded in his programming, and goes on the run with a mysterious teenager who may be his reincarnated son. Matalas serves as showrunner and a director.

rows.title: War in Heaven (novel)
rows.description: 1930 novel written by Charles Williams
rows.summary: War in Heaven is a 1930 novel written by Charles Williams. It is the first of his supernatural novels that C. S. Lewis styled "spiritual shockers" and T. S. Eliot called "supernatural thrillers". The novel traces a humble Anglican priest's struggle with a satanic cabal who are bent on stealing the Holy Graal and using it for dark magic.

rows.title: Watford Grammar School for Boys
rows.description: School in Watford, Hertfordshire, England
rows.summary: Watford Grammar School for Boys is an 11–18 boys academy in Watford in Hertfordshire, England. The school and its sister school, Watford Grammar School for Girls, descend from a Free School founded as a charity school for boys and girls by Elizabeth Fuller in 1704.

rows.title: Waupeton, Iowa
rows.description: Unincorporated community in Iowa, United States
rows.summary: Waupeton is an unincorporated community in Dubuque County, Iowa, United States.

rows.title: Wichita Collegiate School
rows.description: Private school in Wichita, Kansas, US
rows.summary: Wichita Collegiate School, known locally as Collegiate, is a private, co-educational, non-denominational, and non-profit college preparatory day school founded in 1963 currently enrolling 966 students from preschool through 12th grade located in Wichita, Kansas, United States. The Head of School is Nathan Washer, who was appointed in July 2019. The school motto is: "Proba te Dignum"

rows.title: William
rows.description: Male given name
rows.summary: William is a masculine given name of Germanic origin. It became popular in England after the Norman conquest in 1066, and remained so throughout the Middle Ages and into the modern era. It is sometimes abbreviated "Wm." Shortened familiar versions in English include Will or Wil, Wills, Willy or Willie, Bill, Billie and Billy.

rows.title: Winter (dolphin)
rows.description: Bottlenose dolphin (2005–2021)
rows.summary: Winter was a bottlenose dolphin at the Clearwater Marine Aquarium in Clearwater, Florida, United States, and was widely known for having a prosthetic tail. Winter was the subject of the 2009 book Winter's Tale, the 2011 film Dolphin Tale, and its 2014 sequel.

rows.title: Wonderblocks
rows.description: British children's TV series
rows.summary: Wonderblocks is a British animated television series for preschoolers that debuted on CBeebies on 20 January 2025. The series follows the adventures of block characters in Wonderland, each one being part of a different group. Together with the series Alphablocks, Numberblocks and Colourblocks, it is a part of the "Blocks Universe". Commissioned by the British Broadcasting Corporation, the programme was created by Joe Elliot and David Bowman, and produced by Alphablocks Ltd. with Blue Zoo Animation Studio.

rows.title: Xi Jinping
rows.description: Leader of China since 2012
rows.summary: Xi Jinping is a Chinese politician who is the paramount leader of China. He has served as the general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and chairman of the Party Central Military Commission (CMC) since 2012, and as the president of China and chairman of the State Central Military Commission since 2013.

rows.title: Yannick Cahuzac
rows.description: French footballer (born 1985)
rows.summary: Yannick Cahuzac is a Corsican former professional footballer who played as a defensive midfielder. He is currently the manager of Ligue 1 club Lens. In his career, he played for Bastia, Toulouse, and Lens.

rows.title: Yarabí Ávila Gonzalez
rows.summary: Yarabi Avila Gonzalez is a Mexican politician who served as the Secretary of Education for Michoacán from 2021 to 2022, and the President of the Red Juntos for Michoacan directive since 2023.

rows.title: Yee Leng Xiong
rows.description: American politician
rows.summary: Yee Leng Xiong is an American community organizer and Democratic politician from Wausau, Wisconsin. He is the Treasurer-elect of the state of Wisconsin.

rows.title: Ysgol Llangennech
rows.description: School in Carmarthenshire, Wales
rows.summary:
Ysgol Llangennech is a Welsh primary school located in Llangennech, Carmarthenshire. It was previously two schools, Ysgol Babanod Llangennech and Ysgol Iau Llangennech. These amalgamated in 2017 when the school became Welsh-only.

rows.summary: Élisabeth Louise Vigée Le Brun, also known as Louise Élisabeth Vigée Le Brun or simply Madame Le Brun, was a French painter who mostly specialized in portrait painting, in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

queries.CLOCK:
MATCH (ev:Event)
RETURN max(ev.started_at) AS started, max(ev.ended_at) AS ended
queries.SEARCH_ENTITIES:
CALL db.index.fulltext.queryNodes('qa_entity_names', $query)
YIELD node
RETURN node.key AS key, node.name AS name, coalesce(node.aliases, []) AS aliases,
       node.type AS type, node.wikidata_id AS wikidata_id
LIMIT $limit
queries.SEARCH_PAGES:
CALL db.index.fulltext.queryNodes('qa_page_titles', $query)
YIELD node
RETURN node.title AS title
LIMIT $limit
queries.EVENTS:
MATCH (ev:Event) WHERE ev.key IN $keys
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Page)-[po:PART_OF]->(ev)
WITH ev, p, po ORDER BY po.score DESC
WITH ev, [x IN collect({title: p.title, revision: po.revision}) WHERE x.title IS NOT NULL]
     AS pages, max(po.score) AS score
RETURN ev.key AS key, ev.title AS title, ev.description AS description,
       ev.started_at AS started_at, ev.page_count AS page_count, pages,
       ev.status AS status, ev.ended_at AS ended_at, score
ORDER BY ev.started_at DESC
queries.EVENTS_BETWEEN:
MATCH (ev:Event) WHERE ev.started_at >= $start AND ev.started_at < $end
RETURN ev.key AS key ORDER BY ev.page_count DESC, ev.started_at DESC LIMIT $limit
queries.TRENDING:
MATCH (ev:Event) WHERE ev.status = 'active' OR ev.started_at >= $since
OPTIONAL MATCH (:Page)-[po:PART_OF]->(ev)
WITH ev, max(po.score) AS score
RETURN ev.key AS key
ORDER BY ev.page_count DESC, score DESC, ev.started_at DESC LIMIT $limit
queries.PAGE_TEXT:
MATCH (p:Page) WHERE p.title = $title OR toLower(p.title) = toLower($title)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[po:PART_OF]->(ev:Event)
WITH p, po, ev ORDER BY ev.started_at DESC
WITH p, [x IN collect({revision: po.revision, key: ev.key}) WHERE x.key IS NOT NULL] AS parts
WITH p, parts, [x IN parts WHERE x.key = $event] AS own
RETURN p.title AS title, p.description AS description, p.summary AS summary,
       CASE WHEN size(own) > 0 THEN own[0].revision ELSE parts[0].revision END AS revision,
       [x IN parts | x.key][..5] AS events
ORDER BY p.title = $title DESC LIMIT 1
queries.EVENT_OVERVIEWS:
MATCH (ev:Event) WHERE ev.key IN $keys
WITH ev, properties(ev) AS props
RETURN ev.key AS key, ev.title AS title, ev.description AS description,
       COUNT { (:Entity)-[:INVOLVED_IN]->(ev) } AS entities,
       props['extracted_at'] AS extracted_at,
       CASE WHEN props['briefing'] IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE coalesce(props['briefing_written_at'], props['extracted_at']) END
         AS briefing_written_at,
       props['briefing_verified'] AS briefing_verified,
       props['briefing_model'] AS briefing_model,
       coalesce(props['briefing_sources'], []) AS briefing_sources,
       coalesce(props['briefing_urls'], []) AS briefing_urls
queries.ENTITIES_BY_KEY:
MATCH (n:Entity) WHERE n.key IN $keys
RETURN n.key AS key, n.name AS name, coalesce(n.aliases, []) AS aliases,
       n.type AS type, n.wikidata_id AS wikidata_id
queries.ENTITY_EVENT_COUNTS:
MATCH (n:Entity) WHERE n.key IN $keys
RETURN n.key AS key, COUNT { (n)-[:INVOLVED_IN]->(:Event) } AS events
queries.EVENTS_BY_NUMBER:
MATCH (ev:Event) WHERE ev.number IN $numbers
RETURN ev.key AS key ORDER BY ev.started_at DESC
queries.PAGE_EVENTS:
MATCH (p:Page)-[:PART_OF]->(ev:Event) WHERE p.title IN $titles
RETURN p.title AS title, collect(ev.key) AS keys
queries.ENTITY_EVENTS:
MATCH (n:Entity {key: $key})-[r:INVOLVED_IN]->(ev:Event)
RETURN n.key AS entity_key, n.name AS entity_name, r.type AS type, ev.key AS event_key,
       ev.title AS event_title, r.source_title AS source_title,
       r.source_revision AS source_revision
ORDER BY ev.page_count DESC, ev.started_at DESC LIMIT $limit
queries.EVENT_ENTITIES:
MATCH (n:Entity)-[r:INVOLVED_IN]->(ev:Event {key: $key})
RETURN n.key AS entity_key, n.name AS entity_name, r.type AS type, ev.key AS event_key,
       ev.title AS event_title, r.source_title AS source_title,
       r.source_revision AS source_revision
ORDER BY r.confidence DESC, n.name LIMIT $limit
queries.ENTITY_RELATIONS:
MATCH (n:Entity {key: $key})-[r:RELATED_TO]-(m:Entity)
OPTIONAL MATCH (ev:Event {key: r.event_key})
RETURN startNode(r).name AS subject, r.relation AS relation, endNode(r).name AS object,
       r.event_key AS event_key, ev.title AS event_title,
       r.source_title AS source_title, r.source_revision AS source_revision
ORDER BY r.confidence DESC, ev.page_count DESC LIMIT $limit
queries.EVENT_RELATIONS:
MATCH (a:Entity)-[r:RELATED_TO {event_key: $key}]->(b:Entity)
OPTIONAL MATCH (ev:Event {key: $key})
RETURN a.name AS subject, r.relation AS relation, b.name AS object,
       r.event_key AS event_key, ev.title AS event_title,
       r.source_title AS source_title, r.source_revision AS source_revision
ORDER BY r.confidence DESC LIMIT $limit
queries.PATHS:
MATCH (a:Entity {key: $a}), (b:Entity {key: $b})
MATCH p = allShortestPaths((a)-[:RELATED_TO|INVOLVED_IN*..4]-(b))
RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | coalesce(n.name, n.title)] AS names,
       [r IN relationships(p) | {
          start: coalesce(startNode(r).name, startNode(r).title),
          end: coalesce(endNode(r).name, endNode(r).title),
          label: CASE type(r) WHEN 'INVOLVED_IN' THEN 'involved in' ELSE r.relation END,
          source_title: r.source_title, source_revision: r.source_revision}] AS steps
LIMIT $limit
